title: Sum of products — multiplication is inside the terms
note: The multiplications are inside the terms, already done. The last operation applied to the whole expression is addition — a sum.

pitfalls.why: the × is the most visible operation, so students name it first

title: Product containing a sum — looks like a sum
note: The + is trapped inside a chunk (the bracket). The dominant operation is the multiplication outside — a product.

pitfalls.why: the + inside the bracket is the most visible operation

title: Coefficient in front of a power
note: 2x² is 2·(x²), not (2x)². The power applies to x only; the dominant operation is the product of 2 and x². Connects to notation D3/D4.

pitfalls.why: it reads like (2x)², taking the coefficient to be part of the base

title: Expression with a leading minus
note: A leading minus is just the sign of the first term — it does not make the whole thing a subtraction. -3x + 2y is a sum. (A leading minus can also sit on a power, e.g. -(x+1)², which is a power then negated.)

pitfalls.why: the leading minus looks like subtraction

title: Power containing a sum
note: The base is the whole chunk (x+1). The dominant operation is the power.

pitfalls.why: the + inside the bracket is visible
the implicit multiplication in 3x looks dominant

title: Quotient with a complex numerator or denominator
note: The sums are inside the chunks (numerator and denominator). The whole thing is a division — a quotient.

pitfalls.why: the sums inside the numerator and denominator are visible
